column4: Visit note | 2026-01-04 02:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Ashraf Hasan, 69, male. Mr. Hasan returns for review complaining that his breathlessness has worsened over several days, accompanied by more sputum than usual and his long history of smoking. He works as a tailor and notes his symptoms flared after rubbish was burned near his home in Tongi. He denies chest pain or fever. On examination: SpO2 90%, BP 115/86 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 92 kg. Chest examination reveals diffuse wheezing and prolonged expiration. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued for necessary medications. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.
